channel.title: what a ridiculous universe
channel.description: New items from the sources I follow, merged into one feed.

item.title: Recovering the History of Anti-Zionist Judaism
item.description: Author Benjamin Moser delves into the long tradition of Jewish dissent against Israel and the logic of ethnic nationalism.

item.title: The Road to Socialism Runs Through the State Legislatures
item.description: State government doesn’t get much media attention, but few institutions have more potential to bring about progressive change.

item.title: Don’t Let JD Vance Weasel Out of This
item.description: The Trump administration has the Loser Stink, and Vance is looking to wash it off. But as vice president, he owns the GOP’s failure.

item.title: The Myth of “Red States” Has Collapsed
item.description: There is no such thing as a red state. The toxic Republican Party can be defeated everywhere. But Democrats have to show they can deliver. If they squander this moment, it will be short-lived.

item.title: Riding the Rails With America's Last Train-Hoppers
item.description: In an age of surveillance and hyper-connectivity, a secretive subculture still finds freedom in the open road.

item.title: Israel’s Elections, Like Ours, Show How Much the Parties Agree On
item.description: In both countries, the debate is about how—not whether—to conduct imperial violence.

item.title: Don’t Let Medicare For All Be Rebranded
item.description: From Current Affairs

item.title: Centrists Are Not More "Electable"
item.description: Whether a candidate can inspire people, organize them, and deliver for them matters more than where they stand on an imaginary ideological continuum.

item.title: How Fiction Shows the Possibilities of Radical Environmental Activism
item.description: From Edward Abbey’s The Monkey Wrench Gang to the “ecotage” novels of today, literature helps us grapple with the enormity of the planet’s crisis—and how far we’d go to solve it.

item.title: Kyle Kulinski on Bill Maher, Abdul El-Sayed, and America’s War Crimes
item.description: The host of “Secular Talk” previews his next Current Affairs article...

item.title: What South Africans Know About Elon Musk
item.description: I grew up under apartheid. Musk and his father Errol, technologists and race fanatics, transmit its warped perspectives to the world.

item.title: Angie Nixon and the Unexpected Surge of Progressivism in Florida
item.description: Florida’s politics have been misunderstood. Democrats have failed to compete there because they haven’t offered voters inspiring candidacies, not because it’s a “red” state.

item.title: A Seaside Shrine to the Slaveholders' Insurrection
item.description: Jefferson Davis is the only traitor with a "presidential library"—and you paid for it. My visit to America's most appalling tourist attraction...

item.title: Traveling Route 66 in the Age of Data Centers
item.description: Driving through America’s back roads, the emptiness of the information superhighways comes into sharp relief.

item.title: “Zero Parades” is Missing the Politics That Made “Disco Elysium” Great
item.description: Sold as the successor to “Disco Elysium,” “Zero Parades: For Dead Spies” is well-executed, but lacks the soul of studio ZA/UM’s debut effort.

item.title: Why Don’t Americans Protest Like the French?
item.description: Across France, a mass protest and strike movement has nearly brought the state to its knees. In the U.S., there are things we can learn from our European counterparts.

item.title: The Sick World of Body Camera YouTube
item.description: Police body cameras were meant to hold officers accountable. On YouTube and beyond, they’ve become a wildly profitable form of human misery as entertainment.

item.title: The Art of Ambushing Members of Congress
item.description: Drop Site News reporter Julian Andreone spends his days staking out the hallways of the Capitol, confronting congress members on the issues they'd rather avoid—and you can too.

item.title: Starship Troopers Is the Perfect Movie for the Trump Presidency
item.description: Paul Verhoeven's classic depiction of a militarist fascist society helps demonstrate how propaganda works and what it conceals.

item.title: Our Times Make “Idiocracy” Look Like Utopia
item.description: The problem with our era is not the stupidity, but the sadism.

item.title: No Kings. No Demands. What Happened?
item.description: Behind the scenes, the organization leading America’s largest anti-Trump protests has declined to endorse impeachment—and pressured local organizers who demand it.

item.title: It’s Time to Ban Prescription Drug Ads
item.description: The United States is one of the few countries that allow advertising to prescription drugs. It’s adding billions to our healthcare costs.

item.title: Capitalists Don’t Take On “Risk,” Workers Do
item.description: We’re often told business owners deserve their profits because of the “risks” they take. Nonsense.

item.title: Before Bernie and Mamdani, There Was Eugene Debs
item.description: Historian Shawn Gude on his new biography of one of the 20th century’s most fascinating political figures.

item.title: American Colonialism Lives on in Guam
item.description: U.S. military power has poisoned Guam’s waters, controlled its politics, and prevented its people from determining their own future.
